title: November 22 catch-up — ShadowValley, HeadAsResonator3 and Theorem
summary: Three late November 22 repositories missing from the earlier five-node curation: transformer look-away/complement readings; phase-preserving audio-to-electrode measurements with common-average-reference controls; and difference-aware identifiability using active probes and sensor-calibration failure cases. Existing Nov 22 inverse/cabbage nodes are linked, never duplicated.

nodes.claim: Ports HEAD's eight-slot zero-sum 'look away' trap to small attention layers, gives an analytic optimal-readout error geometry, and tests unsigned residual-guided routing against matched misleading-teacher controls.
nodes.survived: On the constrained attention-only scalar-cue task, plain softmax gets stuck looking away in 6/20 runs and an unsigned teacher solves 20/20 for both target signs; attention maps can hide exact complement reading.
nodes.killed: A standard pre-LN block showed no corresponding look-away traps in the examined runs; richer queries and different attentions change the failure. Results are tiny synthetic CPU models, not an explanation of arbitrary real LLM heads.

nodes.claim: Phase-preserving transfer-function and lagged-model microscope compares speaking-microphone signals with multichannel public EEG recordings, with shifted-input nulls and rereferencing interventions.
nodes.survived: Real Gate 003B finds strong held-out audio-related electrode prediction in 5/9 recordings across 2/3 participants; common-average referencing removes 88–96% of positive raw mean R² in those five recordings, supporting a substantial shared recorded component.
nodes.killed: The original eight-new-person Gate 003 failed eligibility: only one new participant was available. Microphone-to-electrode coherence does not identify a skull resonance, neural pathway or audio source; recording and reference effects remain confounded.

nodes.claim: Integrates ShadowValley, Luotain2 and HeadAsResonator3 into difference-aware identifiability: candidate laws must differ in directions excited by the input and preserved by the measurement; explores controlled interventions and noisy field-law inference.
nodes.survived: Gate 003 recovered all six known wormhole-law spatial terms in 20/20 flat-spectrum 48-probe trials, with zero false links in 60 null runs. Gate 008 detected an Allen–Cahn cubic term in 27/40 held-out synthetic worlds with targeted pulses vs 1/40 white-noise pulses.
nodes.killed: This is an algorithmic test of known SVD/experiment-design geometry, not a new universal theorem. Active broadband white outperformed candidate-directed probes in earlier linear search, and a nonlinear detector fabricated false physical cubic laws in 21/40 targeted Gate 008 cases until an idealized independent sensor was supplied.

edges.why: ShadowValley explicitly ports the HEAD zero-sum look-away toy into attention layers and tests the complementary reader.
Both use candidate lag proposals, held-out evaluation and noise/mixing restraint; the audio-electrode code is ordinary FIR estimation, not Luotain2's spatial-law learner.
Theorem explicitly uses ShadowValley's zero-sum complement case as one of its three identifiability laboratories.
Theorem explicitly incorporates reference-induced ambiguity in audio/electrode source attribution.
Theorem explicitly takes Luotain2's weak-excitation and hidden-wormhole laws into controlled active interventions and sensor-noise checks.

motifs.title: A missing law may be a missing excitation or an untrustworthy measurement
motifs.description: ShadowValley exposes how zero-sum structure permits a misleading complement read; HeadAsResonator3 identifies reproducible microphone-linked signals but not their physical path; Theorem deliberately stimulates discriminating directions but also demonstrates detector-induced false nonlinear laws. Observability and true causality must be separated.
